payload.milestone_description:
Let $n\ge1$ and $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n$. For $0\le i<n$, let $r_i:[t_i,t_{i+1}]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Write
$$D_+r_i(t)=\liminf_{s\to t^+}\frac{r_i(s)-r_i(t)}{s-t}.$$
Assume $r_0(0)\ge-6$, and, for each $i<n$ and $t_i\le t<t_{i+1}$,
$$D_+r_i(t)\ge\frac23r_i(t)^2.$$
At every internal joining time, assume $r_i(t_{i+1})\le r_{i+1}(t_{i+1})$ for $i+1<n$. Then
$$r_i(t)\ge-\frac6{1+4t}\qquad(0\le i<n,\ t_i\le t\le t_{i+1}).$$
This isolates the scalar comparison step used in Kleiner-Lott's surgery estimates, with upward jumps allowed. Applying it to scalar-curvature minima requires establishing these analytic hypotheses from the geometry; this statement does not itself formalize a Ricci flow.

[Source: Kleiner-Lott, proof of Lemma 79.11, p. 154](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=154), using [Appendix B, equations (B.1)-(B.2), p. 202](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=202).

payload.milestone_description:
For vectors $v,w$ in a real inner product space, define the area density and energy density by

$$A(v,w)=\sqrt{\|v\|^2\|w\|^2-\langle v,w\rangle^2},\qquad E(v,w)=\frac{\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2}{2}.$$

Let $(X,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $v,w:X\to F$ be almost-everywhere strongly measurable fields with integrable energy density $x\mapsto E(v(x),w(x))$. Then

$$\int_X A(v(x),w(x))\,d\mu\leq\int_X E(v(x),w(x))\,d\mu.$$

No finiteness assumption on the measure is needed; finite energy is explicit. This isolates the analytic ingredient in the surface area-energy comparison. Identifying the vector fields with the differential of a Sobolev surface map, and proving invariance under changes of orthonormal frame, are separate geometric tasks.

payload.milestone_description:
Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, with $n\ge1$. Fix $p\in M$, $K\in\mathbb R$ and $0<r_1\le r_2$. Assume that the geodesic ball $B_g(p,r_2)$ has compact closure in $M$ and that on this ball

$$\operatorname{Ric}_g(v,v)\ge(n-1)K\,g(v,v)$$

for every tangent vector $v$. If $K>0$, also require $r_2\le\pi/\sqrt K$. Define

$$s_K(t)=\begin{cases}\sin(\sqrt K\,t)/\sqrt K,&K>0,\\t,&K=0,\\\sinh(\sqrt{-K}\,t)/\sqrt{-K},&K<0,\end{cases}\qquad V_{K,n}(r)=\int_0^r s_K(t)^{n-1}\,dt.$$

Then the Riemannian volumes of the concentric geodesic balls satisfy

$$\frac{\operatorname{vol}_g(B_g(p,r_2))}{\operatorname{vol}_g(B_g(p,r_1))}\le\frac{V_{K,n}(r_2)}{V_{K,n}(r_1)}.$$

This is the Riemannian Ricci-lower-bound version of the comparison in [Kleiner-Lott, Appendix G, equation (G.1) and the following paragraph, pp. 211-212](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=211). The factors used to normalize $s_K$ cancel in the ratio. It supplies a comparison-geometry input to the [surgery noncollapsing estimates, Sublemma 79.23, p. 157](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=157).

**Verified analytic prerequisites.** [Integral comparison on nested lower intervals](https://prove2.me/theorems/1b1a2764-46a8-4ccb-9220-d38a56f8a6a5); [Radial density comparison implies integrated comparison](https://prove2.me/theorems/0c4bdb95-16b2-4bf0-ba4d-e7177b1dcebb); [Monotonicity of normalized radial integrals](https://prove2.me/theorems/00a47c26-3e61-4afc-91c7-117708e1baf9). The first two results preserve the DifferentialGeometry proofs; the third is an OpenGA corollary. These establish the integral comparison step. The full geometric milestone remains open: geometric density comparison, polar integration, the ball-local hypotheses and positive model curvature still require a faithful platform development.

**Verified model definitions.** [Model radial function and density for nonpositive curvature](https://prove2.me/theorems/5f12b4eb-73fe-4f5b-9eca-ea195943cb23); [Radial model volume for nonpositive curvature](https://prove2.me/theorems/8f010cd2-75b6-40f7-abdf-ec788a788a40). They are used in [Radial integral monotonicity with the model-volume denominator](https://prove2.me/theorems/58a8c735-04e5-4c94-afef-0b03d5d80e0a), connected to the earlier integral comparison proof. This model batch covers curvature $K=-q^2\le0$ and uses radial exponent $d=n-1$. The angular constant cancels in ratios. The geometric milestone remains open, and this analytic component is not yet a dependency of the Poincare goal theorem.

payload.milestone_description:
Fix $\alpha,K>0$, $K'\ge0$, $l\ge0$ and positive integers $m,n$. There is a constant $C=C(\alpha,K,K',l,m,n)$ with the following property. Let $r>0$ and let $g(t)$ solve Ricci flow on an open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M^n$ for $0\le t\le\bar t$, where $0<\bar t\le\alpha r^2/K$. Assume that the closure of the time-zero ball $B_{g(0)}(p,r)$ is a compact subset of $U$, and that

$$|\operatorname{Rm}(x,t)|\le K/r^2\quad\text{on }U\times[0,\bar t],\qquad |\nabla^\beta\operatorname{Rm}(x,0)|\le K'/r^{|\beta|+2}\quad(x\in U,\ |\beta|\le l).$$

Then, for $x\in B_{g(0)}(p,r/2)$, $0<t\le\bar t$ and $|\beta|\le m$,

$$|\nabla^\beta\operatorname{Rm}(x,t)|\le\frac{C}{r^{|\beta|+2}(t/r^2)^{\max(m-l,0)/2}}.$$

The source's $K=0$ case has identically zero curvature, so all the indicated derivatives vanish. The displayed positive-$K$ formulation makes the time bound unambiguous. The case $l=0$ is Shi's estimate; the source also includes initial derivative control for $l\ge0$.

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Appendix D, Theorem D.1 and equations (D.2)-(D.4), p. 207](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=207).

payload.milestone_description:
Let $g(t)$, $0\le t<T$, be a smooth Ricci flow on a three-manifold, with complete time slices and curvature bounded on every compact time interval. Use the curvature-operator convention in which constant sectional curvature $k$ gives the operator $2k\,\mathrm{Id}$ on two-forms; its trace is the scalar curvature $R$.

Write its eigenvalues as $\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\lambda_3$ and assume $\lambda_1(x,0)\ge-1$ for every $x$. At any spacetime point with $X=-\lambda_1(x,t)>0$,

$$R(x,t)\ge X\bigl(\log X+\log(1+t)-3\bigr).$$

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Appendix B, equation (B.3) and its hypotheses, pp. 202-203](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=203). This curvature-operator estimate supplies the pinching input used to obtain almost nonnegative curvature in blowup limits.

payload.milestone_description:
Consider smooth Ricci flows $g_i(t)$ on connected pointed $n$-manifolds $(M_i,p_i)$, defined for $t\in(A,B)$, where $-\infty\le A<0<B\le\infty$. Assume that every $(M_i,g_i(0))$ is complete and that the injectivity radii at $(p_i,0)$ have a common positive lower bound.

For each compact interval $I\subset(A,B)$, require a finite constant $N_I$ such that, for every $r>0$, there is an index $J_{r,I}$ for which

$$i\ge J_{r,I}\ \Longrightarrow\ \sup_{B_{g_i(0)}(p_i,r)\times I}|\operatorname{Rm}(g_i)|\le N_I.$$

The curvature bound $N_I$ is independent of $r$; the starting index may depend on $r$.

Then a subsequence converges smoothly in the pointed sense to a Ricci flow on a connected pointed manifold $(M_\infty,p_\infty)$, defined on the same interval $(A,B)$, with complete time slices. Convergence is through time-independent pointed identifications on compact spatial and time subsets.

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Appendix E, Corollary E.4, pp. 208-209](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=208).

payload.milestone_description:
Let $(M^n,g(\tau))$, $0\le\tau<T$, be a connected complete backward Ricci flow, $\partial_\tau g=2\operatorname{Ric}$, with curvature bounded on compact time intervals. Fix a basepoint $p$ at $\tau=0$. For $\tau>0$, define the reduced length by

$$l_p(q,\tau)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt\tau}\inf_{\gamma(0)=p,\,\gamma(\tau)=q}\int_0^\tau\sqrt{s}\left(R(\gamma(s),s)+|\dot\gamma(s)|_{g(s)}^2\right)\,ds,$$

using the admissible curves of the source's $\mathcal L$-length construction. Define the reduced volume with Kleiner-Lott's normalization by

$$\widetilde V_p(\tau)=\int_M\tau^{-n/2}e^{-l_p(q,\tau)}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g(\tau)}(q).$$

This integral is finite, and for $0<\tau_1\le\tau_2<T$,

$$\widetilde V_p(\tau_2)\le\widetilde V_p(\tau_1).$$

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Section 23, pp. 43-44](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=43), using [equations (15.1), (15.3)-(15.4) and the construction in Section 17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=33). The time variable is backward time; this source does not include a $(4\pi)^{-n/2}$ prefactor in $\widetilde V$.

payload.milestone_description:
For every positive integer $n$, $0<T<\infty$ and $\rho,K,c>0$, there is $\kappa=\kappa(n,K,c,\rho,T)>0$ with the following property. Let $g(t)$ solve Ricci flow on $M^n$ for $0\le t<T$, with curvature bounded on $M\times[0,T']$ for every $T'<T$. Assume that $g(0)$ is complete, $|\operatorname{Rm}(g(0))|\le K$ everywhere, and $\operatorname{inj}(M,g(0))\ge c$.

Whenever $0<r<\rho$, $r^2\le t_0<T$, and

$$|\operatorname{Rm}(x,t)|\le r^{-2}\quad\text{for all }x\in B_{g(t_0)}(x_0,r),\ t\in[t_0-r^2,t_0],$$

one has

$$\operatorname{vol}_{g(t_0)}B_{g(t_0)}(x_0,r)\ge\kappa r^n.$$

With $n,K,c,\rho$ fixed, $\kappa$ can be chosen nonincreasing in $T$. The curvature hypothesis uses the entire backward parabolic region over the fixed final-time ball.

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Definition 26.1 and Theorem 26.2, p. 47](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=47).

payload.milestone_description:
Fix $\kappa>0$. Given any sequence of oriented three-dimensional $\kappa$-solutions and basepoints $(x_i,0)$, apply parabolic dilations so that $R(x_i,0)=1$. A subsequence then converges smoothly in the pointed sense to an oriented three-dimensional $\kappa$-solution with scalar curvature one at its basepoint at time zero.

Here a $\kappa$-solution has the meaning of Definition 38.1: it is ancient; its time slices are complete; its curvature is bounded on each compact time interval; its curvature operator is nonnegative; its scalar curvature is everywhere positive; and it is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at all scales. Solutions based at time zero are considered on their common ancient interval $(-\infty,0]$. All these conditions, including bounded curvature on compact time intervals, hold for the limit with the same $\kappa$.

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Theorem 46.1 and its normalization in the proof, p. 81](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=81); [Definition 38.1, p. 67](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=67).

payload.milestone_description:
Let $\Phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)$ be positive and nondecreasing, with $\Phi(s)/s$ decreasing to zero as $s\to\infty$ through positive values. For every $\epsilon,\kappa,\sigma>0$, there exists $r_0>0$ with the following property.

Let $g(t)$ be a Ricci flow on a three-manifold for $0\le t\le T$, $T\ge1$, with complete time slices and sectional curvature bounded on compact time intervals. Suppose all sectional curvatures at $(x,t)$ are at least $-\Phi(R(x,t))$, and the flow is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at scales below $\sigma$ in the parabolic sense of Definition 26.1.

For any $(x_0,t_0)$ with $1\le t_0\le T$ and $Q=R(x_0,t_0)\ge r_0^{-2}$, the flow on

$$\{(x,t):d_{g(t_0)}(x,x_0)^2<(\epsilon Q)^{-1},\quad t_0-(\epsilon Q)^{-1}\le t\le t_0\}$$

is, after parabolic rescaling by $Q$ and moving $t_0$ to zero, $\epsilon$-close in the source's smooth spacetime sense to the corresponding region of a $\kappa$-solution. The fixed noncollapsing scale $\sigma$ is independent of the resulting threshold $r_0$.

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Definition 52.1, Theorem 52.7 and Remark 52.8, pp. 89-90](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=89); smooth closeness is clarified in [Definition 58.1, p. 108](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=108).

payload.milestone_description:
Fix the source's sufficiently small global parameter $\epsilon$, including the pinching convention preceding Lemma 79.12. Given $\epsilon\ge r_-\ge r_+>0$, $\kappa_->0$, $E_->0$ and finite $E>0$, there are positive constants

$$\bar\delta=\bar\delta(r_-,r_+,\kappa_-,E_-,E),\qquad\kappa_+=\kappa_+(r_-,\kappa_-,E_-,E)$$

with the following property. Let $0\le a<b<c$, $b-a\ge E_-$ and $c-a\le E$. Consider a Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff, as in Definition 73.1, with normalized initial data and a domain containing $[a,c)$. Assume

- $r(t)\ge r_-$ on $[a,b)$ and $r(t)\ge r_+$ on $[b,c)$, with $r(t)\le\epsilon$;
- the flow is $\kappa_-$-noncollapsed below scale $\epsilon$ on $[a,b)$;
- $\delta(t)\le\bar\delta$ on $[a,c)$.

Then it is $\kappa_+$-noncollapsed below scale $\epsilon$ on $[b,c)$. Crucially, $\kappa_+$ can be chosen independently of $r_+$, although $\bar\delta$ may depend on it.

Here normalized initial data means a compact initial three-manifold with $|\operatorname{Rm}|\le1$ and each unit ball having at least half the volume of the Euclidean unit ball. Noncollapsing is the surgery convention of Section 77: for $0<\rho<\epsilon$ and $t\ge\rho^2$, an unscathed backward parabolic neighborhood $P(x,t,\rho,-\rho^2)$ with $|\operatorname{Rm}|\le\rho^{-2}$ has $\operatorname{vol}B(x,t,\rho)\ge\kappa\rho^3$. The cutoff-flow hypothesis includes the source's pinching and canonical-neighborhood assumptions and prescribed surgery procedure.

Source: [Kleiner-Lott, Lemma 79.12 and Remark 79.13, p. 154](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=154); [Definition 73.1, p. 139](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=139); [normalization and noncollapsing conventions in Section 77, p. 146](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=146).
